metadata.title: The Watermark Is One Line of Code
metadata.subtitle: A git-explainer walkthrough of jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking — the KGW reference implementation
metadata.purpose: Walk the jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking GitHub repo with real git/wc data. Show that the marking mechanism is one line of code, that detection returns a p-value not a verdict, and that a commit labelled 'Documentation Updates' silently changed the detection statistic. Rung 1 throughout — all data from the local clone at books/lm-watermarking HEAD 8292251.

beats.narration_text: Hola — this is Liam, in for Bear. Anthropic says Claude's text carries a watermark. I cloned the reference implementation for this whole family of techniques. Can you walk me through what the mark actually is?
beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer — ask lands answered: 16 commits, KGW family, the mark is one line of code.

props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code
output: The mark is one line of code.

beats.narration_text: The watermark is a statistical bias, not an inscription. At generation, half the vocabulary gets a two-logit boost at every token position. At detection, a z-test asks whether too many boosted tokens appeared by chance. The algorithm is 282 lines. The surrounding apparatus is 344,000 lines of file. The detection returns a p-value. A p-value is not a verdict.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — BLUF on cream stage; key numbers on screen

lines: Statistical bias, not inscription. No token is modified.
Generation: +2.0 logits on half the vocabulary at every position.
Detection: z-test on green token count → p-value, not a verdict.
The algorithm: 282 lines. The apparatus: 344,000 lines of file.

beats.narration_text: The word watermark comes from images, where there is a thing in the file you could point at. There is no such thing in the text. Nothing here is embedded.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — conceptual reframe: visible mark vs statistical bias

lines: Image watermark: a thing in the file you can point at.
Text watermark: a statistical property of token choices.
Nothing is embedded. No token is changed.
The mark is in the distribution, not in the data.

beats.narration_text: The repository: jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking. Official implementation of the 2023 ICML paper by Kirchenbauer and colleagues. Sixteen commits since the first push. Built on the HuggingFace transformers LogitsProcessor abstraction — the hook that intercepts probability distributions before sampling.
beats.new_visual_element: GitHubRepoHero — repo identity, 16 commits, LogitsProcessor tagline

props.name: lm-watermarking
props.headline: Official implementation of A Watermark for Large Language Models
props.tagline: Built on the HuggingFace transformers LogitsProcessor abstraction

beats.narration_text: LogitsProcessor matters. It doesn't reach inside the model. It sits between the model's output distribution and the sampling step, and it adjusts logits. The model's weights are unchanged. The watermark lives in the selection rule — which token the sampler picks — not in any parameter.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — LogitsProcessor intercept diagram (text)

lines: model output → LogitsProcessor → adjusted logits → sampler
LogitsProcessor does not touch the model's weights.
The watermark is in the selection rule, not in a parameter.

props.headline: Three functions. The key. The bias. The test.

beats.narration_text: Five parameters. gamma: 0.5 — half the vocabulary is green at each position. delta: 2.0 — the logit boost applied to green tokens. hash_key: 15485863 — the secret, described in the code as 'just a large prime.' seeding_scheme: simple_1 — the RNG seeds on the single previous token only. z_threshold: 4.0 — the detector's decision boundary.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — parameter table: γ, δ, hash_key, seeding_scheme, z_threshold

lines: gamma = 0.5          — green list is half the vocabulary
delta = 2.0          — logit boost for green tokens (L37-38)
hash_key = 15485863  — the secret: 'just a large prime' (L40)

beats.narration_text: Three functions. First: how the key and the previous token seed a fresh random partition of the vocabulary at every position.

props.command: Animate the KGW green list: 50,257-token vocabulary grid, γ=0.5 → 25,128 green tokens. Show the partition reshuffling at each of 6 successive token positions — same grid, new coloring each time.
props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code

beats.narration_text: At every token position, the mechanism draws a fresh random permutation of the full vocabulary — seeded by the secret key and the previous token. The first half of that permutation is the green list. It changes completely at the next position. It is never stored. There is no green list file anywhere in this repository.

production_viz.note: γ=0.5 verified at watermark_processor.py L37. No gen-AI. Teardown palette.

beats.narration_text: The seeding and partitioning code. Line 63: the previous token times hash_key seeds the RNG — that is the entire secret. Line 74: torch.randperm shuffles the full vocabulary using that RNG. Line 76: the first gamma-fraction of the shuffle is the green list. Range shortened to L62–80: L61, the assert, overflows the frame at the type floor — see BUILD-LOG.md.

beats.narration_text: Now show the bias — high entropy versus low entropy.
beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk ASK — logit bars before Manim B27

props.command: Show logit distributions before and after applying +2.0 delta to green tokens. Two panels: high entropy (uniform-ish distribution — token choice flips with the boost) and low entropy (peaked distribution — top token wins regardless, Barack → Obama case).
props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code
output: B27_LogitBars.mp4 — high vs low entropy bias

beats.narration_text: When the model is uncertain — high entropy, multiple near-equal options — adding 2.0 to the green logits shifts which token is sampled. Choice flips. When the model is confident — Barack followed by Obama — the top token wins regardless of the green boost. The watermark is invisible at low entropy. It only bites when there is a real choice.
beats.new_visual_element: Manim B27_LogitBars — two panels: high entropy (choice flips with +δ) vs low entropy (top token holds)

production_viz.label: Logit bias: high vs low entropy
production_viz.mechanic: Left panel: ~6 bars near equal height (high entropy). Apply +2.0 to green bars: one green bar surpasses the previous argmax — sampled token changes. Right panel: one dominant bar (low entropy, Barack→Obama). Apply +2.0 to green bars: argmax unchanged — token holds. Teardown palette.
production_viz.note: delta=2.0 verified at watermark_processor.py L38. green bars in terracotta, red bars in warn. No data invented.

beats.narration_text: Line 95: scores on the green list get plus greenlist_bias — which is delta, which is 2.0. That is the entire marking mechanism. Everything else in __call__ is batch handling, RNG setup, and the calls to the seeding and masking functions.

lines: def __call__(self, input_ids: torch.LongTensor, scores: torch.FloatTensor) -> torch.FloatTensor:
# this is lazy to allow us to colocate on the watermarked model's device
# NOTE, it would be nice to get rid of this batch loop, but currently,
# the seed and partition operations are not tensor/vectorized, thus
# each sequence in the batch needs to be treated separately.
props.caption: L95–117 · L95 is the watermark: +greenlist_bias on green scores (range shortened: L94 def overflows frame)

beats.narration_text: scores[greenlist_mask] = scores[greenlist_mask] + greenlist_bias. That is the watermark. One line. Add two to half the logits.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — dark card: the one line, isolated

lines: That is the watermark. One line.
Add two to half the logits.

beats.narration_text: Now the test. 200 tokens versus 40.
beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk ASK — binomial null before Manim B31

props.command: Plot the binomial null distribution for γ=0.5 at T=200 tokens. Mark the z_threshold=4.0 boundary. Show a realistic watermarked observed count and its z-score. Then repeat for T=40 tokens — show that the test has no statistical power to detect.
props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code

beats.narration_text: Detection is a hypothesis test. Under the null — no watermark — approximately gamma times T tokens fall green by chance. The z-statistic measures how many standard deviations above chance the observed count sits. At 200 tokens, the test has power — a watermarked text clears the z_threshold of 4.0. At 40 tokens, the distribution is wide and the same observed count does not clear the threshold. The test returns a p-value, not a ruling.
beats.new_visual_element: Manim B31_BinomialNull — binomial null at T=200 (detection) vs T=40 (no power); z=4.0 boundary marked

production_viz.label: Binomial null vs observed: 200 vs 40 tokens
production_viz.mechanic: Left panel T=200: narrow binomial distribution centered at γT=100. Observed count (e.g. 118) marked; z-score computed; arrow to z=4.0 threshold — observed exceeds it. 'DETECTED'. Right panel T=40: wide distribution centered at γT=20. Same observed fraction: z-score below 4.0 threshold — 'INSUFFICIENT POWER'. Teardown palette.
production_viz.note: gamma=0.5 (L37), z_threshold=4.0 (L125) verified. Binomial math correct. No data invented.

beats.narration_text: Lines 153–163. The z-score: observed green count minus expected, divided by the binomial standard deviation. The p-value: scipy.stats.norm.sf — the survival function, one-tailed area above z. This function returns a float. The threshold comparison happens in the caller.
beats.new_visual_element: GitHubCodeViewer — Slice C, L153-164, watermark_processor.py, branch main

lines: # count refers to number of green tokens, T is total number of tokens
props.caption: L153–164 · z-score: binomial deviation · p-value: scipy.stats.norm.sf(z)

beats.narration_text: Detection is scipy.stats.norm.sf(z). It returns a p-value. A p-value is not a verdict, and asking to see the watermark is like asking to see the loadedness of a single die roll.

beats.new_visual_element: GitHubSectionRail — kicker: THE CHANGE

props.headline: A commit that said 'Documentation Updates' and wasn't.

beats.narration_text: Commit bbe1fb8. August 2023. Message: 'Documentation Updates.' The stat for watermark_processor.py: seventeen lines added, fifteen removed. Most of it is genuine cosmetics — blank lines, PEP8 comment spacing. But one line is not documentation.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — commit metadata card: bbe1fb8, Documentation Updates, +17 -15

lines: Most of it: blank lines, PEP8 spacing.

beats.narration_text: Buried in the WatermarkDetector __init__ signature: the default value of ignore_repeated_bigrams changed from False to True. That is not documentation.
beats.new_visual_element: GitHubCodeDiff — bbe1fb8 key section: ignore_repeated_bigrams False → True in WatermarkDetector.__init__

props.caption: bbe1fb8 · 'Documentation Updates' · WatermarkDetector.__init__ · the key line

beats.narration_text: Seventeen lines added, fifteen removed, message 'Documentation Updates.' One of them flipped a detector default from False to True. The key line is where the error hides.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — dark verdict card: the specific failure of the commit message

lines: The key line is where the error hides.

beats.narration_text: ignore_repeated_bigrams changes how observed_count is computed — whether repeated token bigrams get counted once or every time they occur. That changes the z-score. That changes the p-value. That changes the detection verdict for any text that sits near z_threshold of 4.0. A commit labelled 'Documentation Updates' changed the detection statistic.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — consequence chain: ignore_repeated_bigrams → observed_count → z-score → p-value → verdict

lines: → changes: detection verdict for texts near z_threshold=4.0

beats.narration_text: The verdict: the algorithm is honest. The mechanism is 282 lines and it does exactly what the paper says. But the mismatch between what the README recommends and what the tree imports is a real gap — and the commit that said 'Documentation Updates' changed the scoring rule. If you audit a text and the detector says no, you are reading a p-value above 4.0, not a ruling. The watermark is statistical. So is the doubt.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this into your own session: clone jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking, open watermark_processor.py, and ask Claude what happens to detection power when you raise delta from 2.0 to 5.0 — and what the model quality trade-off looks like at high delta. Then ask what z_threshold controls, and what a false positive looks like at 200 tokens with no watermark present. Liam, in for Bear.
